themes.label: Neo-Memphis
themes.note: Cream dotted ground, near-black ink, 2px black edges with 6px pink offset shadow, 0.75rem radius, teal #007f79 temperature, Poppins.

themes.label: Singapore Sky
themes.note: The only theme that reads data. data-sky on <html> from skyState(): storm (thunder now or in the period covering now) > haze (24h PSI > 100) > heat (NEA High WBGT, station within 10 km) > calm (also when data is missing). White ink, 85% ink-muted, 1.125rem radius, flat panels, system font stack, NEA flag pills and banded gauges, focus ring #ffe14a, selected pin #5eead4.

calm.trigger: default, and whenever a reading is missing

storm.trigger: thunder in the current condition or the forecast period covering now
storm.materials: cloud base 70%, violet underlight, rain sheets 10%, one-shot sheet lightning

haze.materials: smoke veil 17%, dull sun disc 12%, panels frost at blur(32px) saturate(0.7)

heat.trigger: NEA High heat stress from a WBGT station within 10 km
heat.materials: horizon burn 30% from the bottom edge

sky.contrast: 85% ink clears 4.5:1 on a selected (20%) card at the sky's lightest point, effective material alphas included; rain masked out of the hero reading; worst case haze 4.58:1.

singapore.psi: hard bands at 50 / 100 / 200 of 300: green, yellow, orange, red
singapore.wbgt: hard bands at 31 / 33 over 25-35 °C: green, yellow, red
singapore.uv: hard bands at 2 / 5 / 7 / 10 of 11: green, yellow, orange, red, purple

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Doorstep Glance"**

Every screen is designed for the moment just before someone steps outside. They have a few seconds and one hand free. The page answers with one large reading: the place name, a very large hairline-weight temperature, and the day's high and low with the time of the last update. Everything below it is quieter and lighter, and holds back until the user wants more detail. Hierarchy comes from size and how strong the ink is. Colour carries very little of it.

The default Apple theme puts frosted, translucent panels over a gradient of the day's sky, slate blue going darker towards the bottom. One ink colour (white in Apple) does all the work. Text, borders, fills and dividers are that same ink at different opacities, so the panels look like part of the sky rather than objects placed on top of it. Components are quiet but tactile. At rest they are faint frosted panels with hairline edges. When pressed or selected they clearly brighten and lift, and on touch screens every control is big enough for a thumb.

The visual identity sits in a swappable set of CSS variables, while the layout stays fixed. Five alternative themes (Apple Glass, Midnight Radar, Pastel Sticker, Neo-Memphis, Singapore Sky), six themes in all, replace the materials completely and keep the same structure and hierarchy. Apple is the reference theme. It changes only in deliberate theming work.

Singapore Sky is the only theme that reads data. Its ground is not a fixed palette but the selected place's sky, repainted from that location's stored snapshot so the page answers "can I go out?" before any number is read. Four dark Singapore skies, chosen in strict precedence storm > haze > heat > calm: a bruised-violet 3 pm storm under a lumpy cloud base with slanted rain sheets (thunder in the current condition, or in the forecast period covering now); a smoky sepia haze with a smoke veil and a dull sun disc (24-hour PSI above 100); a scorched rust heat burning up from the bottom edge (NEA High heat stress from a WBGT station within 10 km); and a blue-grey calm with cumulus heads, which is also the answer whenever a reading is missing, so the sky never guesses. White ink, NEA flag colours on the heat-stress pills and banded gauges, and the system font stack: its character comes from the sky and the flags.
keyCharacteristics: One huge, hairline-weight current temperature (6.5rem, weight 200) is the single focal point.
One ink colour, used at different opacities, makes every text colour, border and fill.
Translucent frosted panels with a 1rem radius and a hairline edge, with no shadow at rest.
Small, wide-tracked uppercase labels name each panel. The data, not the labels, does the talking.
Colour is reserved for data scales (UV, air quality, heat stress, temperature range) and map markers.
Phone first: the whole page scrolls on phones, controls are 44px or larger, and Refresh sits within thumb reach.
In Singapore Sky the ground itself is a reading: one of four sky states, crossfaded through registered colour tokens, with a single one-shot lightning flicker as its only authored motion.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Every foreground colour is the theme's ink at some opacity. Never hard-code white, grey or slate for text or borders. Map overlay buttons take their colours from the theme's `--map-control-*` tokens.

rules.name: The Colour Means Data Rule
rules.body: Saturated hues encode a measurement (UV, PSI, heat stress, temperature range) or a map marker. They are never used for decoration, branding or emphasis.

rules.name: The Flag Text Exception
rules.body: NEA flag pills in Singapore Sky are the one scoped exception to the One Ink Rule. White ink cannot be read on green or yellow, so the Low flag uses fixed dark text (`flag-text-green`) and the Moderate flag fixed dark text (`flag-text-yellow`). The High flag keeps white on `flag-red`, with a light 1px border (white at 55%) because red on the dark sky is under 3:1 as an edge. The exception covers only these pills. It is consistent with the Colour Means Data Rule, since in this theme the flags and the sky itself carry data.

rules.name: The Sky Is Data Rule
rules.body: In Singapore Sky the ground is a measurement. It changes only through `skyState()` (storm > haze > heat > calm, calm when data is missing), never for decoration, time of day or mood. A new sky state needs a data trigger and a place in that precedence.

rules.name: The Lightest-Point Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every Singapore sky state is budgeted so that 85% ink clears 4.5:1 on a selected (20%) card at the sky's lightest point, with each material's effective alpha included. Rain is masked out of the hero reading. The worst case is haze at 4.58:1, so any brighter material or lighter stop must be rechecked against this budget.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every temperature, time, high/low and measurement uses `tabular-nums`, so values don't shift sideways when they update.

rules.name: The One Giant Rule
rules.body: Only the hero temperature is set at display size. Other numbers stay at title size or smaller, so the main reading is never in doubt.

rules.name: The Fixed Order Rule
rules.body: The order of the content is the same on every theme and every screen size. Phones change how things are shown (chips instead of cards, a floating Refresh), never what comes first.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: In Apple, panels have no shadow at rest (`--card-shadow: none`). A shadow is a sign of state or of floating, never decoration.

rules.name: The Opaque Pop-up Rule
rules.body: Anything that floats over content (pop-ups, the floating Refresh) uses an opaque surface (`--popover-bg`), because translucent fills let the content underneath show through.

rules.name: The Quiet Low Rule
rules.body: In the hero's one-line summary only Moderate and High heat get a flag pill. Low stays plain text so it never outshouts a storm. The WBGT tile shows all three bands as flags.

dos: Do derive every foreground colour from the ink token (`text-white/…`, `border-white/…`, `bg-white/…`), which follows the theme.
Do mark every themeable panel with `rounded-card`, so all six themes can restyle it.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or larger on phones, and keep Refresh and location switching within thumb reach.
Do show every reading with its update time and source, and use "--" for missing values.
Do use `tabular-nums` for every number that can change.
Do use the opaque pop-up surface (`--popover-bg`) for anything that floats over content.
Do give every gauge a `scale` and let the theme's `--scale-*` token fill it; in Singapore Sky, band it at the NEA cut-offs.
Do change a Singapore sky material by changing its colour token, so it crossfades; keep every material in the stack at all times.
Do recheck the lightest-point budget (85% ink at 4.5:1 on a 20% card, effective alphas included) whenever a sky stop or material gets brighter.
donts: Don't change how the Apple theme looks as a side effect of other work. It changes only in deliberate theming work that follows Apple's current design language.
Don't use saturated colour for decoration or emphasis. It is reserved for data scales and map markers.
Don't put a second display-size number on the screen, or make the hero temperature heavier in Apple.
Don't add shadows to panels at rest in Apple.
Don't hard-code white, grey or slate text. Map overlay buttons use the `map-control` tokens.
Don't use translucent `bg-white/…` fills for pop-ups or floating controls.
Don't extend the flag-text exception beyond the NEA flag pills; everything else in Singapore Sky is ink.
Don't flag Low heat in the hero summary, or let rain cross the hero reading.
Don't add a second authored motion to Singapore Sky, or loop the lightning.
